description:
FILED s543i (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22), found by the full gate run on a `git archive` extraction (scratch/s543i/x-final, a directory INSIDE the s543i git worktree): Pl/t/pcl-runtime-env-01.t row 1 FAILS there and passes in the checkout.

    got:      v0.1.0-3239-gafbfc7c7 (git checkout)          <- the runtime, %p-pcl-version (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~9488)
    expected: unknown (no VERSION file, and not a git checkout)   <- `pcl --version`, pcl_version() (pcl ~413)

Two derivations of ONE string disagree, although the runtime's docstring says "SAME SOURCE, not a second one":
(1) `pcl` asks `git describe` only when ROOT itself holds `.git` (`-d "$ROOT/.git" || -f "$ROOT/.git"`); `%p-version-from-git` runs `git -C ROOT describe` unconditionally, and git walks UP to an enclosing repository -- so a PCL tree nested inside some other git checkout (an extraction, or a user who vendors PCL into his own repo) reports THAT repository's describe as PCL's version;
(2) with no VERSION and no git the runtime answers "unknown" where `pcl` answers "unknown (no VERSION file, and not a git checkout)" -- so the row fails in ANY tree that is neither installed nor a checkout (a plain tarball extraction outside any repo too, by the second difference).
Fix (cl/, one place): give %p-pcl-version the same two tests and the same fallback text as pcl_version() -- or better, have one of them read the other's answer.  Guard: run Pl/t/pcl-runtime-env-01.t in a `git archive` extraction both inside and outside a git checkout.
subject: DIVERGENCE (tooling, minor): $ENV{_PCL_RUNTIME_}'s version string and `pcl --version` are two derivations that disagree outside a checkout -- the runtime runs `git describe` without checking ROOT/.git (a tree nested in another repo reports THAT repo) and falls back to "unknown" without the reason; Pl/t/pcl-runtime-env-01.t row 1 fails in an extraction
triage_reason: a version string in a diagnostic variable, not program semantics; the gate row fails only outside a checkout or an install
